title: Texas Instruments worker given unknown metal

tellings.quote: You know a famous example is the infographic show whistleblower where he talks about a guy at Texas Instruments getting a piece of metal and not knowing what he's working on.

plain: A worker at the electronics company Texas Instruments was supposedly handed a piece of metal to study without being told what it was or what he was working on. A guest who goes by UAPGerb mentions it to Michels as "a famous example" of reverse engineering, meaning taking apart recovered technology of unknown origin to learn how it works. He did not hear it himself: he repeats it from an anonymous source known as the Infographics Show whistleblower. If true, it would mean strange material was being farmed out to ordinary engineers who were kept in the dark.
